title: Sora: Video Generation as World Simulation
hook: OpenAI's Sora generates minute-long high-fidelity video from text by treating video as space-time patches - and frames the whole task as learning a world simulator.
key_points: Combines a diffusion model with a Transformer to denoise sequences of space-time patches.
Handles variable durations, resolutions, and aspect ratios in a single unified model.
Can maintain consistent objects, lighting, and camera motion across long clips.
OpenAI frames Sora as an implicit world model, not just a video synthesizer.
content_html: OpenAI announced Sora in February 2024, a model capable of generating video clips up to a minute long from text prompts. It operates on compressed space-time patches of video, applying a diffusion process guided by a Transformer backbone.
extra_html:
How it works

Sora encodes video into a compact latent space, then represents it as a sequence of space-time patches - analogous to how Vision Transformers treat images as patch tokens. A diffusion Transformer learns to denoise these patch sequences, conditioned on text. Because patches are resolution- and duration-agnostic, the same model can produce video at many sizes and lengths without retraining.

Why it matters

Beyond visual quality, OpenAI's framing is notable: they argue that predicting consistent video requires learning something like a model of the physical world - physics, occlusion, object permanence. Whether or not that claim holds up scientifically, Sora raised the bar for what generative video models can produce. See the full technical report on OpenAI's site for example outputs and architectural details.

related.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)
related.hook: Running diffusion on raw pixels is brutally expensive. Do it in a compressed latent space instead, and high-res text-to-image becomes cheap enough to run on a consumer GPU.

related.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words (ViT)
related.hook: Chop an image into patches, treat each like a word, and feed them to a plain Transformer. With enough pretraining data, it matches or beats convolutional networks.

related.title: Classifier-Free Guidance
related.hook: Want a diffusion model to follow your prompt more closely? Blend its prompt-aware and prompt-blind predictions — no extra classifier required. That's the guidance-scale slider.
